citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The attending veterinarian’s (AV’s) site visits have not been performed at the frequency agreed upon in the written
Program of Veterinary Care (PVC). The current PVC states the attending veterinarian will have regularly scheduled visits
annually. The licensee said the AV contacts him to schedule the annual visit and he had no current plans to contract the
AV himself. Inspectors consulted with the AV who said his last visit to the facility was on October 10, 2025 and he had not
reached out to the licensee to schedule a date, nor did he have any specific date in mind for an annual visit.
Not following the prescribed frequency of regularly scheduled veterinary premises visits can lead to an inadequate
standard of veterinary care for the animals. The licensee shall ensure the correct frequency of regularly scheduled AV
visits occurs as prescribed in the written Program of Veterinary Care.
Correct by: November 6, 2026.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility is not using appropriate methods to prevent diseases. The written Program of Veterinary Care (PVC) specifies
that all incoming regulated animals must be quarantined prior to being introduced into the established animal population.
Facility employees told inspectors that they quarantine animals by keeping them in a separate enclosure in the same
room as the established animal population. Inspectors consulted with the attending veterinarian (AV) who stated that his
intention in the written instruction were for new animals to be housed in a separate room from existing animals while being
quarantined. Additionally, the facility is feeding a parakeet seed diet to the budgies as their sole diet. The AV told
inspectors that he verbally instructed the facility to feed a balanced pelleted diet because all-seed diets are nutritionally
incomplete and will lead to malnutrition in budgies.
Failure to follow veterinarian instruction on quarantine may allow the spread of infections and infestations, leading to
illness or death of animals. Failure to follow veterinarian instruction on proper feeding in parakeets may lead to vitamin
deficiencies, liver disease, skeletal abnormalities, injury, or death.
Correct by November 6, 2026 by following the PVC and verbal instruction from the AV on the use of appropriate methods
to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility is not conducting adequate daily observations of gerbils to accurately assess their health and well-being, nor is
it promptly reporting all findings to the Attending Veterinarian (AV). In one enclosure containing seven gerbils, one animal
had both eyelids visibly swollen to the point where inspectors couldn't see the gerbil's eyes. The eyelids stayed swollen
and shut throughout several minutes of handling by a facility employee. A second gerbil exhibited almost circumferential
hair loss extending several millimeters up the bridge of the nose. The exposed skin appeared thickened and reddened.
The enclosure bore a note stating, “one has hurt nose.” Employees reported noticing the gerbil with hairless over the nose
the previous day but failed to promptly notify the AV. Inspectors instructed a facility representative to contact the AV
immediately after the inspection and confirmed that the facility had communicated to the AV the following day.
Lack of direct and timely communication between the facility and the attending veterinarian could lead to treatment delays
which may negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals.
Daily observation of all animals is necessary to assess their health and well-being. If any problems of animal health,
behavior and well-being are noted, they must be conveyed to the attending veterinarian in a timely and accurate manner
to allow for appropriate diagnosis and treatment.
Correct by October 27, 2026.

The facility failed to maintain complete and accurate inventory records of hamsters, birds, guinea pigs, and gerbils. The
facility did not have complete records of all purchases and births of these animals, nor complete records of all sales and
deaths. The inventory records of hamsters, birds, guinea pigs, and gerbils did not match the current inventory and staff
could not explain the discrepancy. Two birds had died the previous week and were not recorded on the inventory.
Correct record keeping is necessary to properly identify animals and to accurately trace animals to ensure their legal
acquisition, health, and humane transportation.
Every dealer shall make, keep, and maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose acquisition and
disposition information regarding animals purchased or otherwise acquired, owned, held, leased, or otherwise in his or her
possession or under his or her control, or which is transported, sold, euthanized, or otherwise disposed of by that dealer.
Correct by October 28, 2026.

The facility is not ensuring hamster enclosures are in good repair, protect the animals from injury, and contain the
animals. One enclosure housing five Syrian hamsters had a gap in the metal mesh covering the enclosure. The gap had
previously been repaired with a metal patch, but the patch was peeling away from the top of the enclosure leaving an
approximately 0.75” gap. Inspectors observed hamsters attempt to stick their heads through the gap.
Gaps and sharp points in enclosures could cause pain and distress if the animals were to escape or be injured.
Correct by October 27, 2026, by ensuring housing facilities for hamsters are structurally sound and maintained in good
repair to protect the animals from injury, to contain the animals, and to restrict the entrance of other animals.

The facility has not established and maintained an adequate pest control program in the room housing hamsters.
Inspectors observed rodent feces and urine on the floor next to hamster food storage bins and bedding material and near
animal enclosures. Live and dead cockroaches were found along the entire room perimeter.During this inspection,
inspectors observed that the facility had attempted to limit pests from entering the room by taping down the plastic
baseboard with packing tape. The packing tape did not hold the plastic to the wall and the baseboard moved away from
the wall easily, revealing a live cockroach. When inspectors showed the licensee the area, the licensee said that he was
aware cockroaches were in the facility but was not able to mitigate them.
Lack of an adequate pest control program can negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals through
contamination of feed and transmission of diseases.
Correct by November 6, 2026 by ensuring that an effective program for the control of insects, ectoparasites, and avian
and mammalian pests is established and maintained.

The facility has not established and maintained an adequate pest control program in the room housing gerbils and ferrets.
Inspectors observed rodent feces and urine on the floor next to gerbil and ferret food storage bins and bedding material
and near animal enclosures. Live and dead cockroaches were found along the entire room perimeter. During this
inspection, inspectors observed that the facility had attempted to limit pests from entering the room by taping down the
plastic baseboard with packing tape. The packing tape did not hold the plastic to the wall and the baseboard moved away
from the wall easily, revealing a live cockroach. When inspectors showed the licensee the area, the licensee said that he
was aware cockroaches were in the facility but was not able to mitigate them.
Lack of an adequate pest control program can negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals through
contamination of feed and transmission of diseases.
The facility must ensure that a safe and effective program for the control of insects, ectoparasites, and avian and
mammalian pests is established and maintained.

An enclosure was not large enough as to allow each bird to make normal postural and social adjustments, nor did the
attending veterinarian consult with the facility to ensure that the space in all the bird enclosures is adequate. Twenty-three
birds were housed in an enclosure approximately 4’ by 2’. Two perches are angled in the enclosure, further limiting perch
space. At one point during the inspection, inspectors observed five of the 23 birds on the bottom of the cage and 2 birds
on the bars. The birds on the bottom of the cage were not foraging during the inspection. Inspectors consulted with the AV
who stated that the size of the enclosure is not adequate for 23 birds and that he had not been consulted about the
enclosure prior to its use.
Lack of ability to make normal postural and social adjustments may cause malnutrition, poor condition, stress, or
abnormal behaviors.
Each bird must be able to make normal postural and social adjustments with adequate freedom of movement and
freedom to escape from aggression demonstrated by other animals. The AV must consult with the facility to ensure that
the space in all enclosures housing birds is adequate and allows for normal postural and social adjustment.
Correct by October 27, 2026.

citations.desc: Environment enhancement to promote psychological well-being.
citations.narrative:
The facility is not following their written veterinarian-approved avian environmental enhancement plan (EEP). The EEP
states that birds should be provided with perching of varying thicknesses, that ladders and ropes should be installed in
avian cages, and that misting of birds should happen at least twice weekly. The four bird enclosures present in the facility
do not contain any varying sized perches, nor ladders or ropes. Inspectors did not observe any misters in the facility.
Inspectors observed that all bird enclosures contained little to no enrichment through materials or activities. The EEP
states that hook-billed birds should receive cuttlebones and romaine lettuce. Lovebirds are present and did not have any
cuttlebone and were not receiving romaine lettuce.
Birds have complex needs which, if unmet, may cause stress, boredom, and the development of abnormal harmful
behaviors. The environmental enhancement program aims to create and maintain a structured plan to meet birds’
complex behavioral needs.
The facility must ensure that consistent implementation of the written, attending-veterinarian-approved environmental
enhancement plan is performed to meet the psychological well-being and health of the birds.
Correct by October 28, 2026.

The facility is not placing food and food receptacles in enclosures in a manner that minimizes any risk of contamination by
excreta. A bird enclosure containing 23 budgies had a single food bowl that measured approximately five inches in
diameter and was positioned on the bottom of the enclosure directly under the perches. The majority of the food bowl’s
rim and sides were covered in bird excreta. The facility told inspectors that the food bowl had been cleaned earlier that
day. Only a small part of the bowl would allow the birds to perch to eat without touching excreta.
Failure to appropriately maintain clean food receptacles promotes unsanitary surfaces that can harm the birds’ health
upon ingestion of contaminated food.
Food and any food receptacles must be located to minimize any risk of contamination by excreta. Food receptacles and
feeding areas must be kept clean.
Correct by October 27, 2026.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility is not removing excreta and food waste from two of the four bird cages often enough to prevent excessive
accumulation. USDA inspectors observed heavily soiled enclosures lined with newspaper thoroughly covered with
excreta. The sides of the cages had a large amount of encrusted exreta, food waste, and debris the bottom of the cage
and the wire bars.
Failure to maintain clean enclosures creates unsanitary conditions that may jeopardize avian health by increasing disease
risks and attracting pests.
Excreta and food waste must be removed from under and around primary enclosures as often as necessary to prevent
excessive accumulation of waste, to prevent soiling of the birds contained in the primary enclosures, and to reduce
disease hazards, insects, pests, and odors. The facility must clean around the cages and ensure that all cages are
regularly and adequately cleaned on an ongoing basis.
Correct by October 27, 2026.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility has not established nor maintained an adequate pest control program in the room housing birds. Inspectors
observed rodent feces and urine on the floor next to avian food storage bins and bedding material and near animal
enclosures. Live and dead cockroaches were found along the entire room perimeter. During this inspection, inspectors
observed that the facility had attempted to limit pests from entering the room by taping down the plastic baseboard with
packing tape. The packing tape did not hold the plastic to the wall and the baseboard moved away from the wall easily,
revealing a live cockroach. When inspectors showed the licensee the area, the licensee said that he was aware
cockroaches were in the facility but was not able to mitigate them.
Lack of an adequate pest control program can negatively impact the health and well-being of the animals through
contamination of feed and transmission of diseases.
Correct by November 6, 2026 by ensuring ensure that a safe and effective program for the control of insects,
ectoparasites, and avian and mammalian pests is established and maintained so as to promote the health and well-being
of the birds and reduce contamination by pests in animal areas.
This inspection was conducted with the licensee and facility representatives. A complete exit briefing with the licensee and
a facility representative was not conducted due to the licensee ending the briefing abruptly.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
